title: TREATAS over two columns filters the pairs, not each column on its own
query: EVALUATE ROW ( "Pairs", CALCULATE ( [Sales Amount], TREATAS ( { ( "Red", "Vehicles" ), ( "Blue", "Accessories" ) }, Product[Color], Product[Category] ) ) )

source.quote: TREATAS can be used with tables with multiple columns
source.supports: TREATAS takes one target column per column of the table

source.quote: You can also use TREATAS with two or more columns
The number of columns specified must match the number of columns in the table expression and be in the same order
source.supports: the columns are matched in order

derivation: (Red, Vehicles) is Bike: Sales rows 1, 5, 7 = 400. (Blue, Accessories) is Lock: rows 4, 6 = 80. 400 + 80 = 480. Helmet is Red and Accessories, but (Red, Accessories) is not one of the pairs.
notes: Two independent filters, Color in {Red, Blue} and Category in {Vehicles, Accessories}, would include Helmet and give 540.
